data.title: Amit Shah urges all parties to support delimitation Bill, calls it historic
data.description:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said all parties should support the Constitution (132nd) Amendment Bill to effect a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats across states and termed it a "historic initiative" to make women strong partners in governance.

In a message posted on X ahead of a special sitting of Parliament beginning next week, Shah said, "Giving women a stronger role in elected representation has been a commitment of the Modi government. With the Union Cabinet's approval of the 132nd Constitution Amendment Bill under Modi's leadership yesterday, the decades-long wait of the country's women is about to end." "The 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, provided through the Nari Shakti Vandan Act, will now become a reality," he said.

 

"All parties should support this historic initiative to make women strong partners in governance," he added.

The government has convened a four-day special sitting of Parliament from November 30, during which it will bring three bills for the implementation of 33 per cent women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies before the 2029 parliamentary elections, including the Constitution (132nd) Amendment Bill.

Shah said at least one-third representation for women in state assemblies will make the policies of states and Union territories more inclusive, while their presence in the Lok Sabha will add a new dimension to policymaking, lawmaking and the setting of national priorities.

"All parties should support this historic initiative to make women strong partners in governance," he said.

The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared the proposed Constitution amendment bill that seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.

The move will pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general elections.

A two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament is a must for a constitutional amendment bill to get cleared. The DMK, the NCP and the BRS, are expected to support the Bill.

The fresh bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased seats. There will be a freeze on seats till 2051.

The bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not be passed as the ruling dispensation could not muster strength in the Lok Sabha.

The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.

data.title: Bird flu confirmed in TN's Coimbatore; culling continues in Cuddalore
data.description:
Avian influenza has been confirmed in this district after samples from a wild bird found dead earlier this month tested positive for (H5N1), following a series of poultry outbreaks in Cuddalore district.

The ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal confirmed that one of the pond herons found dead in Coimbatore on November 18 had died of H5N1 avian influenza, officials said. The dead birds had been found near Ashwin Hospital on Sathyamangalam Road.

Following the confirmation, the Animal Husbandry Department has stepped up surveillance and preventive measures in Coimbatore.

The development comes amid recurring bird flu outbreaks in Cuddalore district over the past month.

 

Authorities have begun culling over 25,000 chickens at a commercial poultry farm in Nochikkadu near Cuddalore after NIHSAD confirmed a fresh outbreak following the death of over 1,000 chickens at the farm earlier this week.

Rapid response teams were deployed to cull the remaining birds and bury the carcasses in disinfectant-treated pits. The affected farm has been sealed and barred from restocking for 90 days, while animal husbandry teams have intensified surveillance in nearby villages.

In Naduthittu village of Cuddalore district, where bird flu was also confirmed, animal husbandry officials initiated measures to cull 3,000 chickens at an affected farm.

Over one lakh birds have been culled across Cuddalore district in the past month in areas including Krishnankuppam, Naduthittu, and Thyagavalli, said sources.

Meanwhile, in Chennai, the Guindy Children's Nature Park (Guindy Children's Park) has been closed to visitors for three days from November 28 as a precautionary measure following the death of 14 birds in its waterbirds enclosure on Friday.

According to a release issued by the Wildlife Warden, Chennai, the exact cause of the deaths is yet to be ascertained, and avian influenza has not been confirmed in the latest incident. Samples such as carcasses, leftover food, water, and soil -- have been sent to the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal for testing, and the results are awaited.

data.title: South states must unite against unfair delimitation: K'taka CM Shivakumar
data.description:
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday said the proposed Delimitation Bill was unfair to southern states, asserting that they would have to collectively raise their concerns to protect their political representation, while also criticising the Centre for not convening an all-party meeting to discuss the issue.

Speaking about his Delhi visit and the delimitation issue, Shivakumar said Karnataka, along with other southern states, would strongly put forward its concerns, adding that the contribution of South India to the country must be recognised.

"Let them do politics. But it is unfair to the southern states. They want to increase the number of seats, and they feel that our southern states will become a minority in the country," he said.

 

He said that the Chief Ministers of Keralam and Telangana would meet on Sunday to discuss the issue and evolve a common position to safeguard the interests of their respective states.

"Tomorrow, all the Chief Ministers are meeting. Satheesan, Revanth Reddy and I are meeting. We will definitely have to put forward our points and protect the interests of our states and South India. South India is giving more strength to the country in every sense. So, they cannot silence our voice. We will speak on that," Shivakumar said.

He also questioned the Centre's approach to the proposed exercise, saying that political parties should have been consulted before moving ahead with the issue.

"We expected them to call an all-party meeting and discuss the issue with our political parties. I think they have not called an all-party meeting. What Siddaramaiah said is also right. They should have called an all-party meeting and discussed it with us," he said.

Asked about Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu's statement on the delimitation issue, Shivakumar declined to comment, saying, "He is an alliance partner, and I definitely don't want to comment on that."

Meanwhile, Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy launched a sharp attack on the Karnataka government, accusing it of failing to acknowledge corruption allegations despite officials allegedly being caught red-handed.

Kumaraswamy said that this "government is shameless in Karnataka. There are many officials being caught red-handed for involvement in corruption, and the chief minister. In today's conference, he says that there is no corruption in this government. This is the height of shamelessness of this government."

Earlier, Kumaraswamy also visited Cloudnine Hospital in Bengaluru's Jayanagar, where a one-and-a-half-year-old child is undergoing treatment after allegedly being administered a heavy dose of anaesthesia four months ago.

Expressing concern over the child's condition, the Union Minister blamed the hospital and its doctors for the child's suffering and alleged that the hospital management was now attempting to present different accounts of the incident.

He said that the alleged medical error had caused severe damage to the child's brain and that the parents were also not being treated properly by the hospital management.

"Because of the mistake of the hospital and the doctors, a one-and-a-half-year-old kid is suffering for no mistake from their parents. Now the hospital is trying to create different stories after the mistake which they made, which is causing huge damage to the brain of a small baby. Even parents are not being properly treated by the hospital management," he said.

Kumaraswamy said that he had instructed the hospital management to ensure that its authorised representatives meet him by 4 pm on Saturday to discuss the child's further treatment and provide clarifications.

"That is why I have instructed the official management of the hospital to bring their authorised people tomorrow by 4 o'clock to discuss further treatment. Parents have been very patient till now and the family and supporters are still maintaining peace. Even after facing so much trouble from the hospital, which is affecting their kid's life," he said.

He further warned that the child would be shifted to another hospital if the management failed to provide satisfactory answers and arrangements for further treatment.

"I have told the management clearly to bring their authorised people within 4 o'clock tomorrow to give proper treatment and further clarifications, or else we will shift the baby to a different place and we are capable of taking care of the baby. We will also ensure that a legal fight against the hospital will be conducted without any miss," Kumaraswamy said.

The Union Minister also said that the family and its supporters had so far maintained peace despite the difficulties faced during the child's treatment.

data.title: Green partnership gives India-Denmark ties distinct character: S Jaishankar
data.description:
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday said the Green Strategic Partnership (GSP) gives India-Denmark relations a distinctive character, bringing together Danish capabilities and India's scale and development priorities, as he held talks with Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen in New Delhi.

Highlighting the importance of the partnership, Jaishankar said the two countries had made progress in areas such as water, renewable energy, power and green shipping, while cooperation in health, food processing, agriculture and science and technology had further strengthened bilateral ties.

"Our Prime Ministers met this May on the margins of the third India-Nordic Summit, and today we have an opportunity to take stock of the progress in our ties, but also issues which were discussed between them. Among, in our agenda, of course, most important is our Green Strategic Partnership, which has given our relationship a very distinctive character. It brings together Danish capabilities and India's scale and development, and whether it's water, renewable energy, power, or green shipping, there is a lot that we are doing in the framework of the GSP," Jaishankar said.

 

He also welcomed Rasmussen's engagements with Indian companies working in emerging and frontier technologies, as well as defence and security, during his visit to Bengaluru.

Emphasising Denmark's role in India's development ambitions, Jaishankar said New Delhi viewed Copenhagen as an important partner in its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

"What I do want to emphasize is, as we work towards a goal of Viksit Bharat, that is developed India by 2047, we do envisage Denmark as a very important partner in that effort. And that is reflected in the fact that we work with you on many of our national missions," he said.

Jaishankar also highlighted the contribution of Danish companies operating in India and welcomed a larger business presence and increased activities in both countries. He said the two governments could facilitate business by addressing issues and challenges faced by companies.

The External Affairs Minister said the two sides would discuss further prospects for cooperation in defence and security, emerging technologies, space, education, skills and mobility. He also called for greater engagement through existing joint working groups and expressed hope for a new joint action plan for 2026-31.

Jaishankar further underlined the importance of India-Denmark cooperation in the broader context of strengthening India-EU relations, appreciating Copenhagen's support for deepening the partnership and concluding the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.

Describing the current international environment as complicated and uncertain, he said the two sides would also exchange views on geopolitical and strategic developments.

Earlier, Rasmussen arrived in New Delhi on Saturday to co-chair the fifth India-Denmark Joint Commission Meeting with Jaishankar at Hyderabad House.

In a post on X, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal welcomed the Danish Foreign Minister and said the meeting would focus on further strengthening the Green Strategic Partnership.

Rasmussen's November 27-28 visit includes engagements aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation in technology, innovation, space, quantum technology and defence.

On Friday, the Danish Foreign Minister visited Bengaluru, where he met representatives of Indian research, technology and industrial institutions, including the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP), quantum technology company QpiAI, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

During his engagements, Rasmussen explored opportunities for collaboration in the space sector, including partnerships between Danish small and medium-sized enterprises and Indian space institutions. At HAL, he was briefed on the use of components supplied by Danish company HBK in India's Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv and Light Combat Helicopter, as well as in research and development testing of the Tejas fighter jet.

Rasmussen also met Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge and representatives of Danish companies operating in the state to discuss Global Capability Centres and India's skilled technology workforce.

"You have an enormous talent pool with exactly the skills that Danish companies are looking for. We are not the only ones trying to attract Indian talent. So, we also want to make Denmark an attractive place for skilled Indian professionals to go for work," he said.

During the Bengaluru visit, Innovation Centre Denmark launched its report, 'Access to Tech Talent in India', examining opportunities for Denmark to recruit skilled Indian professionals amid growing demand for talent.

data.title: RBI steps up gold loan scrutiny as bullion rout signals borrower stress
data.description:
By Siddhi Nayak
 
India’s banking regulator is stepping up scrutiny of the nation’s $247 billion gold-loan sector as a sharp drop in bullion prices erodes the collateral that lenders demand from borrowers, according to people familiar with the matter. 
The Reserve Bank of India’s supervisory officers have reviewed early indicators of stress, asset quality and loan amounts against pledged gold, the people said, asking not to be identified as they are not authorised to speak to the media. 
 
Banks and shadow lenders can lend as much as 85 per cent of the metal’s value, and the RBI has been checking protectively if this is being breached, though no evidence has been found yet, the people said. The RBI did not immediately respond to an emailed query.
 
 
The regulator’s stricter watch coincides with signs of distress among borrowers that shadow lenders spotted in the quarter ended September. An amended rule that barred deferred interest repayment has also contributed to delinquencies. The pressure has mounted as gold collapsed 30 per cent since its January peak, with the rout accelerating in recent weeks on expectations of a more hawkish US Federal Reserve. 
 
A record rally in the precious metal had fanned the borrowing boom. The gold lending industry expanded almost fivefold in five years to ₹23 trillion ($247 billion), with about 60 per cent of the market still informal, according to a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. on Friday. The segment accounts for about 2.5 per cent of India’s bank credit as of September, limiting any systemic risk. 
 
The stress in gold credit portfolios is expected to persist over the next few quarters, the people said.
 
A drop in gold prices can leave loans insufficiently backed, forcing borrowers to pledge additional collateral or repay part of their debt. A prolonged decline increases the risk of delinquencies, potentially leaving lenders including IIFL Finance Ltd. and Bajaj Finance Ltd. exposed to losses.
 
IIFL Finance’s nonperforming assets in the gold portfolio edged higher to 0.9 per cent of total loans as of end-September, from 0.6 per cent in the prior quarter, according to its quarterly result disclosures. At Bajaj Finance, India’s biggest shadow lender, the share of gold loans facing repayment stress rose to 2.02 per cent from 1.87 per cent, filings showed.
 
Piramal Finance CEO Jairam Sridharan said in an analyst call last month that gold loans are emerging as an important area of emerging risk.

data.title: India 3rd largest foreign user of SIAC with 178 parties: Singapore minister
data.description:
India ranks as the Singapore International Arbitration Centre's (SIAC) third-largest foreign user jurisdiction, with 178 Indian parties involved in its arbitrations last year, Singapore's Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs Edwin Tong said on Friday.
 
Speaking at the Indian Council of Arbitration's (ICA) symposium on 'India-Singapore: From Shared Legal Foundations to the Future' in Singapore, Tong highlighted India's growing participation in international arbitration and called for greater innovation by institutions, practitioners and courts to address the complexities of cross-border commercial disputes.
 
He said investors need the assurance that disputes arising from their investments would be resolved fairly, transparently and predictably. India has long been among SIAC's most important foreign user jurisdictions, with Indian counsel and arbitrators also participating in cases that do not involve any Indian parties, he added.
 
 
Tong also highlighted the challenges posed by complex, multi-contract transactions, where interconnected disputes can end up being heard in separate forums, potentially leading to inconsistent outcomes.
 
He called for ways to resolve disputes involving interconnected parties more effectively while preserving the fundamental principle of party consent in arbitration.
 
"Arbitration is built on party consent. So how do we preserve that principle whilst ensuring that interconnected parties and their disputes can be resolved effectively?" he said.
 
"India and Singapore should aspire not merely to succeed in international arbitration, but to make international arbitration better," Tong added.

CJI calls for stronger cooperation

In a video message to the symposium, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant called for greater cooperation between India and Singapore in arbitration, mediation and institutional development.
 
He said the two countries could exchange experiences in institutional design, professional standards, training and technology, while encouraging the early use of mediation to resolve commercial disputes.
 
"Predictability in dispute resolution is not an afterthought to commerce, it is part of the confidence that enables it," the CJI said.
 
Highlighting the economic ties between the two countries, Justice Surya Kant said bilateral trade had increased from about $6.7 billion in 2004-05 to $34.3 billion in 2024-25.
 
Singapore also remains a major source of foreign investment into India, with cumulative foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows of about $174.88 billion between April 2000 and March 2025, accounting for around 24 per cent of India's total inflows, he said.
 
The CJI said India's growing engagement with mediation, including the establishment of the Mediation Council of India, offered further opportunities for cooperation between the two countries. He also highlighted the potential of multi-tiered dispute resolution clauses, which provide for mechanisms such as mediation before arbitration.
 
"Sometimes the best outcome is not a victory for one side, but an agreement that enables both sides to move forward," he said.
 
Referring to the 2024 Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Law and Dispute Resolution between India and Singapore, the first meeting of the India-Singapore Joint Consultative Committee in 2025, and the ICA's India-Singapore ADR Conclave held in New Delhi on September 10, 2026, Justice Surya Kant said bilateral cooperation should be based on reciprocity.
 
"Neither needs to replicate the other's institutional model. The opportunity is to learn from each other. The corridor must be a two-way channel for expertise, professional opportunities and institutional knowledge, measured by the confidence it creates on both sides," he said.

Legal cooperation linked to trade ties

ICA President and Senior Advocate Dr N G Khaitan said a shared legal future between the two countries depended on strong economic and trade ties.
 
He highlighted Singapore's predictable regulatory environment, commercial dispute resolution mechanisms and enforcement of law, noting that the country accounted for about 24 per cent of equity FDI into India.
 
"It is a win-win situation for all of us," Khaitan said.
 
ICA Director General Arun Chawla said the symposium marked 200 years since Singapore's Second Charter of Justice was granted on November 27, 1826.
 
He identified four pillars of the India-Singapore partnership: economy and enterprise; emerging technology; energy and environment; and exchanges and engagement, with trust connecting them.
 
"Commerce needs confidence, investment needs certainty, and both need assurance of justice," Chawla

data.title: Mumbai leads with 43% data centre projects, Hyderabad 2nd: Knight Frank
data.description:
Mumbai accounts for the highest 43 per cent share in the total development pipeline of data centre projects across seven major cities, according to Knight Frank.

Real estate consultant Knight Frank India highlighted that the pipeline of data centre development currently accounts for 80 facilities across seven key markets.

These seven cities are -- Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi-NCR, Chennai and Kolkata.

The consultant said the composition of the data centre facilities pipeline indicates a clear shift towards larger facilities.

Developments above 50 MW account for 55 per cent of the total pipeline in the July-September quarter of this year, reflecting an increased emphasis on larger-format infrastructure across India's key data centre markets.

 

"Mumbai continued to dominate India's data centre development pipeline, accounting for 34 of the 80 pipeline facilities in Q3 2026, or 42.5 per cent of the total," Knight Frank said.

Mumbai, the financial capital, recorded a 9.7 per cent increase from 31 facilities in 2025.

Out of 34 data centre projects in the pipeline in Mumbai, 18 facilities are in the above-50-MW segments.

Mumbai also remained the leading market for facilities above 100 MW, with their number increasing from 10 in 2025 to 15 in the September quarter of 2026.

The city additionally recorded 16 facilities in the 10-50-MW category, the highest among the seven markets, reinforcing its position across both mid-sized and large-format developments.

Hyderabad emerged as the second-largest contributor to the pipeline, with its total increasing from 11 facilities in 2025 to 15 in the September quarter.

The city's growth was led by the above-100-MW category, where the number of facilities doubled from four to eight.

Hyderabad also recorded six facilities in the 50-100-MW segment.

Consequently, 14 of its 15 pipeline facilities, or 93.3 per cent, fall within the above-50-MW categories, making Hyderabad the market with the highest concentration of larger-format developments.

This positions the city as an important emerging destination for large-scale data centre infrastructure, the consultant said.

data.title: Bisleri seeks FSSAI review over conflicting test results for Bengal batch
data.description:
Bisleri International has sought a review by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over conflicting laboratory findings concerning a batch of its packaged drinking water manufactured at its facility in Telipara, Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal.
 
The development comes after the regulator prohibited the sale of the specific batch, identified as PB201, on August 12, 2026, following the detection of coliform bacteria in samples tested by its primary and referral laboratories. The FSSAI has also sanctioned prosecution against the company in the matter, according to reports.
 
“Bisleri International Private Limited had already recalled Batch PB201 of its packaged drinking water at the direction of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which prohibited the sale of the batch on 12 August,” the company said in a statement.
 
 
Bisleri said that while the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample, independent tests commissioned by the company yielded different results.
 
The company said it had separately commissioned testing of samples from the same batch at an FSSAI-recognised laboratory, which found that the sample met the applicable standards for coliform bacteria and other food safety parameters.
 
Samples tested at another independent, FSSAI-recognised laboratory also met the prescribed standards, it added.
 
“The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review. Bisleri calls upon FSSAI to examine the sampling process, testing methodology, laboratory findings and any factors that may have contributed to the variation in results,” the statement said.
 
“We expect this matter to be assessed against the same standards applied across the industry,” the company added, reiterating that it would continue to cooperate with FSSAI to establish the facts.
 
Bisleri said it maintained stringent quality controls involving more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process and asserted that its products remained safe for consumption.
 
This is the second recent instance of regulatory action by FSSAI against Bisleri over the quality of its packaged drinking water.
 
On Sunday, the food regulator said it had sanctioned prosecution against the company following the detection of bromate levels above permissible limits in a sample collected from its Goa manufacturing facility. Subsequent testing by a referral laboratory also flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the regulator.
 
The Goa case relates to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at the company's facility, one of its 143 manufacturing plants.
 
Bisleri had said FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025. Initial testing found that five samples met the applicable standards, while the sixth recorded bromate levels of 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.
 
Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting.
 
The referral laboratory found bromate levels within the prescribed limit but separately flagged the presence of PAHs, the company said.
 
On November 23, FSSAI clarified that bromate levels in the retested sample were below the permissible limit. Bisleri subsequently welcomed the clarification, while pointing out that one of six samples tested in a subsequent round had reported PAHs at 0.144 micrograms per litre. Another sample from the same batch cleared all parameters.
 
The company said it had sought a retest of the PAH findings and that subsequent samples tested by FSSAI across its manufacturing facilities had not reported adverse PAH findings.
 
The two cases involve separate batches and manufacturing facilities, with the latest dispute concerning coliform bacteria in the West Bengal batch and the earlier one involving bromate and PAH findings in the Goa batch.

data.title: Indian markets rebound in November after months of underperformance: HSBC
data.description:
Indian financial markets have staged a broad-based recovery in November, reversing months of underperformance against emerging-market peers as falling crude oil prices, a correction in global artificial intelligence-related investments and renewed foreign fund inflows improved investor sentiment, HSBC Global Investment Research said.

Equities, the rupee and government bonds have all rallied, signalling a shift in market sentiment from risk-off to risk-on.

However, sustaining the gains into 2027 will require stronger domestic growth expectations and an improvement in banking-system liquidity, which could remain constrained as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightens monetary policy amid elevated inflation, the global brokerage said.

"India has moved from risk-off to risk-on. After underperforming the EM Index for most of 2026, Indian markets rebounded in November, outperforming across equities, FX and rates. The recovery was supported by falling oil prices, global investors de-risking from AI names and stronger foreign inflows," it said.

 

India had underperformed emerging markets across equities, foreign exchange and interest rates for much of 2026 before staging a sharp turnaround in November.

The Sensex has gained around 13 per cent month-to-date, while the rupee strengthened to its highest level in eight months, trading below 92.50 against the US dollar.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year government security fell by around 20 basis points, indicating a rally in bond prices despite tightening liquidity conditions.

The recovery has been supported by lower international crude oil prices and global investors reducing exposure to artificial intelligence-related stocks, both of which have helped improve sentiment towards Indian assets and encouraged foreign capital flows.

HSBC said the simultaneous improvement across equities, currency and government bonds, along with a positive correlation between equity and debt returns, points to a broad-based improvement in risk appetite.

The return of foreign investors has been a key factor behind November's market rebound, particularly in equities, although debt markets have also seen improved inflows.

Domestic investors have supported Indian markets over the past few years, helping cushion the impact of foreign portfolio outflows.

"While domestic investors are needed to make sure the markets don't fall, sharp increases in returns are typically led by foreign investor participation," the brokerage said.

HSBC's analysis using the Diebold-Yilmaz framework, which measures the transmission of shocks between different asset classes, found that currencies are the largest net transmitter of market shocks in India.

The latest recovery followed a similar pattern, with the rupee beginning to strengthen around the middle of October, ahead of the broader improvement in other asset classes.

The brokerage's multi-asset analysis suggests that the November rebound was not driven by one isolated market development but reflected improving sentiment across financial markets, with currency movements playing an important signalling role.

HSBC, however, cautioned that external factors alone may not be sufficient to sustain India's market performance in the coming year.

Its proprietary multi-asset model identifies two global and two domestic variables that explain a substantial part of returns across Indian asset classes. The model currently indicates that Indian equities remain undervalued relative to their model-implied returns.

The rupee and government bonds, in contrast, appear broadly fairly valued.

This suggests that equities have greater scope to catch up if the current favourable conditions persist. However, once the valuation gap closes, further gains will depend on an improvement in the variables driving the model's expected returns.

HSBC identifies banking-sector liquidity and expectations of potential economic growth as the two key domestic factors that need to improve.

Liquidity could remain under pressure as the RBI tightens monetary policy in response to elevated inflation, potentially limiting the availability of funds in the banking system.

Consequently, stronger growth expectations will become increasingly important in sustaining investor returns.

The brokerage sees a possible improvement in India's export competitiveness and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows as potential catalysts.

India's goods exports rose 25 per cent year-on-year in the previous quarter, supported by a more competitive currency, trade agreements and exporters expanding into new markets.

HSBC said the increase in exports, alongside early signs of stronger FDI inflows, could help improve expectations of India's longer-term growth potential.

If these trends strengthen, they could provide the domestic economic support needed to sustain higher returns across Indian asset classes in 2027.

However, risks remain, including the possibility of renewed escalation in geopolitical tensions pushing oil prices higher and a revival of volatility in global technology stocks. HSBC remains positive on the AI theme for 2027 despite the recent correction.

Against this backdrop, HSBC's equity strategists remain overweight on Indian equities, citing resilient corporate earnings and more reasonable valuations following the period of underperformance.

The brokerage believes the improvement in valuations, combined with the prospect of sustained earnings growth, provides support for the market despite uncertainties surrounding global conditions and domestic liquidity.

Its rates strategists, meanwhile, have introduced a pay-five-year Non-DeliverableOvernight Index Swap (NDOIS) trade, reflecting expectations of tighter monetary policy amid the RBI's focus on inflation.

In foreign exchange, HSBC's strategists have lowered their USD-INR forecasts for the end of 2026 and 2027, signalling a more favourable outlook for the Indian currency.

The brokerage also prefers the rupee among Asian currencies in the deficit-currency category, reflecting its relative attractiveness in regional foreign-exchange carry trades.

data.title: SC clears way for Hockey India elections on Dec 5, sets aside HC orders
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Saturday paved the way for Hockey India elections scheduled to be held on December 5 and set aside two orders of the Orissa High Court staying the poll process.

A bench of Justices K V Viswanathan and Arun Palli recalled the two show cause notices of Hockey India to Hockey Association of Odisha, which had proposed its reclassification from a permanent member to an associate member.

The bench said grievances of Hockey Odisha will be redressed by a committee headed by ex-apex court judge Justice A K Sikri.

It said the court cannot allow the prospect of players, who are performing so well and training hard on the ground, to be jeopardised, and allowed the election to Hockey India to be held on December 5.

 

On November 18, amid the ongoing internal strife within Hockey India, the Orissa High Court refused to vacate its interim stay on the election process of the governing body, observing that its bye-laws do not empower the secretary general to convene Executive Committee meetings without the orders of the president.

It had dismissed an interlocutory application seeking vacation of the interim stay order passed on November 6.

Hockey India had scheduled its elections for December 5, with the final electoral roll due on November 15 and the nomination process scheduled between November 22 and 24.
